definitions.explanation: Gradually adjusting to new conditions, an environment, or circumstances. Can refer to biological adaptation or personal and social adjustment.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{環境|かんきょう}に{順応|じゅんのう}する。
examples.english: To adapt to a new environment.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもは{大人|おとな}より{早|はや}く{新|あたら}しい{生活|せいかつ}に{順応|じゅんのう}する。
examples.english: Children adapt to a new lifestyle more quickly than adults.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{赴任|ふにん}{先|さき}の{文化|ぶんか}に{順応|じゅんのう}するまで{半年|はんとし}かかった。
examples.english: It took half a year to adjust to the culture at my overseas posting.

notes:
Implies a gradual process of fitting in or adjusting, rather than an instant change.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {環境|かんきょう}に{順応|じゅんのう}する (to adapt to an environment)
- {社会|しゃかい}に{順応|じゅんのう}する (to adjust to society)
- {順応性|じゅんのうせい} (adaptability)

USAGE NOTE:
{順応|じゅんのう} emphasizes a natural, passive process of adjustment — the person gradually fits in. Compare with {適応|てきおう}, which can also mean adaptation but often implies a more active or conscious effort to cope.
